Can a single AI model handle images, video, audio, and robot action predictions simultaneously? Black Forest Labs says yes.

Here are the key developments in AI today.

🤖 Black Forest Labs has released FLUX 3, a multimodal foundation model that learns from images, video, and audio inside a single architecture. It is their first model to ship video, audio, and robot action prediction from one set of weights.

🛡️ Anthropic's Fable 5 update proposes a shared jailbreak-severity framework. The goal is to standardize how safety bypasses are categorized across different AI labs, moving away from subjective vendor interpretations.

🧪 FAIRChem v2 and the UMA universal machine-learning interatomic potential have introduced a unified framework for atomistic simulations. The system uses task-specific calculators for the omol, oc20, and omat domains.

🧠 On the user experience side, Claude users report that the model is now actively refusing to store personal health details in its memory. This represents a shift from previous versions, which users frequently relied on to track symptoms.

These updates highlight a clear divide in modern AI development. On one hand, we are seeing massive steps forward in multimodal architecture and scientific simulation. On the other hand, safety guardrails and memory limitations are directly impacting how everyday users interact with these tools.

Which of these updates do you think will have the biggest impact on your daily workflow?
